title: The repeat weekly shop: why it is slow in Tangelo
question: Why does a repeat shop take a returning customer so long in Tangelo, and what would make it a two minute job?
note: Tangelo, Pippin, Marrow and Sorrel are fictional. Every screen is a schematic drawing made for this example, not a screenshot. All lanes are schematic drawings dated 18 Nov 2026; the labels are what is on each screen. Time was not measured: speed is judged from the screens and taps shown, so two minutes is a target, not a timing. The question is the user's, not the one in the input file.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.means: You can tell what to do next without reading twice.

dimensions.name: Speed
dimensions.means: Few steps and little typing to finish the stage.

dimensions.name: Transparency
dimensions.means: Costs, limits and consequences are shown before they bite.

dimensions.name: Engagement
dimensions.means: It gives a reason to come back or go further.

stages.name: Open the app
stages.finding: Pippin and Marrow put the repeat on Home, while Tangelo starts a returning customer at the catalogue and keeps Reorder under the Orders tab.

lanes.flow: Home leads with a one-tap reorder

notes.t: "Reorder last shop" is the first card under the greeting, with "26 items · $64.10" and a Reorder button on it.
"Last shop: Sunday 8 Nov" dates the order that the card will repeat.
"26 items filled from last shop" confirms the tap filled the basket, the same 26 the Home card promised on screen 1.
The $64.10 total from the Home card is not repeated anywhere on this screen, only line prices and "+ 20 more items".
Every line shows a price and nothing else, so stock is not mentioned at this point.

clarity.why: The reorder card is the first thing on Home, but the basket drops the total.

speed.why: One tap on Reorder turns Home into a filled 26 item basket.

transparency.why: Count and total on the card, then no total and no stock status in the basket.

trust.why: Reorder opens the basket with a Continue button, it does not jump to payment.

engagement.why: Fresh this week and Weekly deals sit below the card, nothing tied to the repeat.

lanes.verdict: The fastest route from Home to a full basket, but the basket forgets the total the card showed.
well: Puts last shop first on Home with its date, count and total.
One tap fills the basket with all 26 items.
wrong: The basket screen shows no total and no stock status.
steal: A Reorder last shop card with item count, total and date at the top of Home.

lanes.flow: Home asks for the slot, then shows usuals

notes.t: "Pick your slot" comes before anything else on Home, and "Held for 15 minutes" says the chosen time is reserved.
"Your usuals" rows carry a rhythm and a status, such as "Every 7 days" and "Due" for oat milk.
The 15 minute hold starts on Home, before the customer has added a single item.

screens.step: Opens usuals, adds what is due

notes.t: Two buttons, "Add the 2 that are due" and "Add all 7", give a partial or a full repeat in one tap each.
No line has a price and there is no total, so the cost of "Add all 7" is unknown.
"7 items · 2 are due" heads a list that shows only five of the seven rows.

clarity.why: Slot first, then usuals, with two plainly worded add buttons.

speed.why: Two screens to add usuals, and the usuals list is seven items, not a whole shop.

transparency.why: The slot hold time is stated, but the usuals carry no prices or total.

trust.why: Holding the slot up front removes a reason for checkout to surprise later.

engagement.why: Due and In 3 days labels give a reason to come back on the item's rhythm.

lanes.verdict: Settles the slot and surfaces what is due on the first screen, but prices are missing from the usuals.
well: Slot is picked and held on Home.
Usuals show how often each item is bought and whether it is due.
One tap adds only what is due, or all of it.
wrong: No prices or total on the usuals list.
The list header says 7 items but shows five rows.
steal: Due and In N days labels on repeat items.
A slot picker with a stated hold time on Home.

lanes.flow: Promo-led Home, Buy again sits low

notes.t: Three promo banners and a product grid sit above "Buy again", which is the last row before the tab bar.
The greeting is "Welcome back" with "Deals picked for you", no name and no address.

screens.step: Scrolls down and opens Buy again

notes.t: Each line says how often it was bought, such as "Bought 5 times" for bananas, next to its price.
The only action, "Add 5 to basket", is an outlined button with no total beside it.
This is a list of items ranked by habit, with no past order or date to repeat whole.

clarity.why: Buy again is a small row under three banners, easy to miss.

speed.why: A scroll, a See all tap and an add that covers five items, not a shop.

transparency.why: Prices and purchase counts per line, but no total for the add.

trust.why: Nothing misleading on these screens, and nothing reassuring either.

engagement.why: Deals give a reason to browse, not a reason to repeat a shop.

lanes.verdict: Shows how often each item was bought, but buries the repeat under promotions.
well: Bought N times labels make the list personal.
Every Buy again line carries a price.
wrong: Buy again sits below three banners and a grid.
The add button is outlined and has no total.
steal: Purchase counts on each repeat line.

lanes.flow: Home is browse-first, Orders holds reorder

notes.t: Home has search, category chips, a delivery banner and six "Popular this week" tiles, and nothing about past orders.
"Free delivery over $40" carries the sub line "Applied at checkout", a promise the later screens have to keep.
A "Reorder last shop" card under the greeting would bring the Sunday orders from the Orders tab onto Home.

screens.step: Finds Orders, the only way to repeat

notes.t: Each order card shows date, item count, total and a Reorder button, such as "23 items · $59.80".
Reorder lives on the Orders tab, the third tab, so the customer must know to leave Home to find it.
Three Sundays in a row (15, 8 and 1 Nov) show a weekly habit that the Home screen on screen 1 ignores.

clarity.why: Home gives no sign that a repeat exists; it starts from the catalogue.

speed.why: A tab change then Reorder; what Reorder fills is not shown on these screens.

transparency.why: Order cards show count and total, Home's delivery promise is unexplained.

trust.why: Nothing surprising here; the screens do not show where Reorder leads.

engagement.why: Popular this week is generic and ignores three weekly orders on record.

lanes.verdict: Order history has everything a repeat needs, but Home never points to it.
well: Order cards carry date, count, total and Reorder.
The weekly rhythm is visible in Orders.
wrong: No route to repeat a shop from Home.
All three Reorder buttons look the same, none is marked as the usual.

best.why: One Reorder tap on Home fills a 26 item basket, with count, total and date shown first.
Slot and due usuals are settled on the first screen.

patterns.name: The repeat is on Home
patterns.text: The returning customer's own history is the first thing below the greeting.

patterns.name: Count and total before the tap
patterns.text: The order to repeat shows how many items and what it cost.

patterns.name: Repeat items carry their habit
patterns.text: Lines say how often they are bought or when they are due.

anti.name: Repeat buried under browsing
anti.text: Promotions, search or popular tiles take Home and the repeat sits lower or on another tab.

anti.name: Repeat list with no total
anti.text: The customer adds items without knowing what they will cost together.

ideal.name: Offer last shop on Home
ideal.text: A card with the date, item count, total and one Reorder button.

ideal.name: Fill the basket, do not pay
ideal.text: One tap opens the filled basket for editing.

ideal.name: Mark what is due
ideal.text: Items bought on a rhythm say whether they are due this week.

gaps.title: No repeat on Home
gaps.today: Home is search, chips, a delivery banner and Popular this week; Reorder sits on the third tab, Orders.
gaps.fix: A Reorder last shop card at the top of Home with date, item count, total and one button.

gaps.title: No sign of what is due
gaps.today: Orders shows three Sunday orders, but no item says how often it is bought or whether it is due.
gaps.fix: Due and In N days labels on repeat items, with an add the due ones button.

stages.name: Build the basket
stages.finding: Pippin and Sorrel tell the customer what changed since the last order at the top of the basket, while Tangelo's basket is names and prices and raises nothing.

lanes.flow: Stock check up front, swap or remove

screens.step: Basket opens with a stock check

notes.t: "2 items out of stock" heads the basket with "Swap or remove before checkout", before the customer reaches payment.
The two missing lines are red and marked "Out", each with "Swap or remove" under the name.
"Continue" is the filled button and "Review swaps" is outlined, so the easy path skips the two problems.
Each swap shows its price, such as "Skyr 900g · $4.90", and "Remove from basket" sits beside them.
The sheet handles Greek yogurt only, so the chicken thighs from screen 1 need a second pass.

clarity.why: The banner says what is wrong and what to do before checkout.

speed.why: A swap is one sheet and one tap, but one item at a time.

transparency.why: Stock and swap prices are shown, the basket total is not.

trust.why: Stock problems surface in the basket, but Continue lets them be skipped.

engagement.why: Swap options keep the shop going, nothing more.

lanes.verdict: Catches stock problems before checkout, but makes skipping them the default button.
well: Out of stock items are flagged at the top of the basket.
Swap choices show their prices.
wrong: Continue is more prominent than Review swaps.
No basket total on either screen.
steal: A basket check banner naming how many items are out, before checkout.
Priced swap choices in a bottom sheet.

lanes.flow: Every line carries a swap preference

blocks: Tap a line to change its rule

notes.t: Every line states its out of stock rule, such as "If out: Do not swap" on porridge oats.
No line says whether the item is in stock today, and there is no total or item count.
"Tap a line to change its rule" is the only instruction, placed above the list.

screens.step: Sets the rule for one line
blocks: If this is out of stock

notes.t: The sheet offers three plain choices: "Swap for similar", "Let me choose a swap" and "Do not swap".
The sheet title "If this is out of stock" does not name the line it is changing.

clarity.why: Rules per line are clear, the sheet does not say which line it edits.

speed.why: Setting a rule means a tap per line; whether rules persist is not shown.

transparency.why: Rules and prices are visible, current stock and the total are not.

trust.why: The customer decides in advance what happens to a missing item.

engagement.why: Nothing on these screens beyond the basket itself.

lanes.verdict: Lets the customer decide what happens to every missing item, but never says what is missing now.
well: An out of stock rule on every line.
Three plain rule choices.
wrong: No current stock status.
No basket total.
The rule sheet does not name its item.
steal: A per line If out rule set in the basket.

lanes.flow: Basket flags price changes, not stock

notes.t: "3 prices changed" heads the basket, and each changed line keeps its old price, such as "was $1.20" for pasta.
All three changes are rises: $1.20 to $1.45, $4.25 to $4.60 and $6.40 to $6.90.
Prices are checked against the last order, but no line says anything about stock.
Subtotal, delivery, "Promo SPRING20" at "-$5.00" and the total are all listed above Checkout.
Five lines on screen 1 plus "+ 12 more items" make 17 lines, against "Subtotal (18 items)" here.

clarity.why: The price change banner and was prices read at a glance.

speed.why: Two screens of scrolling to reach Checkout, nothing to fix along the way.

transparency.why: Price changes and a full breakdown, but stock is not mentioned.

trust.why: Honest about prices, silent on stock, and the item count does not add up.

engagement.why: The promo line rewards the order, nothing else invites more.

lanes.verdict: Tells the customer exactly what got dearer and what they will pay, but says nothing about stock.
well: Flags price changes since the last order.
Full cost breakdown before Checkout, promo included.
wrong: No stock status in the basket.
Line count and item count disagree with no explanation.
steal: A was price under each changed line.
A promo as its own line in the totals.

lanes.flow: A plain list with prices and a total

notes.t: Each line is a name and a price, such as "Whole milk 2L" at "$2.10", with no stock status or swap rule.
Nothing on the basket says where its items came from or whether any price changed.
Subtotal, delivery and total are listed above Checkout, and $56.70 plus $4.50 makes the $61.20 shown.
Delivery is charged at $4.50 on a $56.70 subtotal, with no line saying why.
Six lines on screen 1 plus "+ 17 more items" match "Subtotal (23 items)".

clarity.why: A plain list and a clear Checkout, nothing to decide.

speed.why: A scroll to the totals and one tap, with no problems raised on the way.

transparency.why: No stock, no price changes, and a delivery charge with no reason.

trust.why: Nothing warns of the stock failure seen at checkout or explains delivery.

engagement.why: Nothing on the basket beyond the list and the totals.

lanes.verdict: The totals add up and are shown before Checkout, but the basket raises no problem the order will hit later.
well: Subtotal, delivery and total before Checkout.
Item count matches the lines.
wrong: No stock check.
Delivery charge unexplained.

best.why: Out of stock items are flagged and swapped, with prices, before checkout.
Price rises since the last order are flagged with the old price, and the totals are fully broken down.

patterns.name: Lead the basket with what changed
patterns.text: A banner at the top says what is different since the last order: stock or price.

patterns.name: Decide on missing items in the basket
patterns.text: Swaps or a standing rule are settled before checkout.

patterns.name: Full breakdown above Checkout
patterns.text: Subtotal, delivery and total are listed before the button.

anti.name: Basket silent on stock
anti.text: Nothing in the basket says an item is unavailable, so the problem waits for checkout.

anti.name: Basket with no total
anti.text: The customer edits the basket without seeing what it now costs.

anti.name: A charge with no reason
anti.text: Delivery is charged on a basket above the advertised free delivery threshold, with no line explaining it.

ideal.name: Check the basket on open
ideal.text: A banner lists what is out of stock and what changed price since last time.

ideal.name: Resolve each problem in place
ideal.text: Priced swaps, remove, or a standing If out rule, one tap each.

ideal.name: Show what the customer will pay
ideal.text: Subtotal, delivery, any offer and the total, with a reason for every charge.

gaps.title: The basket does not check stock
gaps.today: The basket is a plain list of names and prices; the two missing items surface only at Place order.
gaps.fix: A basket check banner on open naming what is out, with priced swaps or remove for each.

gaps.title: Delivery charged under a free delivery banner
gaps.today: Home says Free delivery over $40, Applied at checkout; the basket charges $4.50 on $56.70 with no line saying why.
gaps.fix: Apply the offer as its own line, or say on the delivery line why it does not apply.
gaps.benchmarkNote: No app on the board shows a free delivery threshold applied or explained. The screens do not show whether this is a bug or a condition.

gaps.title: No sign of price changes
gaps.today: Lines carry today's price only, so a rise since the last order would go unnoticed.
gaps.fix: A price change banner with the old price under each changed line.

stages.name: Slot and checkout
stages.finding: Marrow's checkout is one tap because the slot was held on Home, while Tangelo leaves the slot and the stock problem to the last step, where the order fails.

lanes.flow: Slot chosen at checkout, then one-page pay

notes.t: The slot is picked only now, and "Today 6pm is full" in red is the first thing the customer learns about it.
Address and card are already filled in: "Deliver to Flat 2" and "Card 4242".
The button reads "Pay $59.60", the same figure as the Total line above it.
The summary repeats the chosen slot, "Tmrw 8am", alongside items and delivery.

clarity.why: Two short screens, each with one obvious button.

speed.why: Slot choice waits until checkout and takes its own screen.

transparency.why: Full summary, slot included, and the amount is on the button.

trust.why: The full slot is flagged before choosing, the total matches the button.

engagement.why: The lane ends at Pay; no confirmation screen is shown.

lanes.verdict: A clean two screen payment with the amount on the button, but the slot is left until the end.
well: Saved address and card.
Pay button names the amount.
wrong: Slot is chosen last, and the first slot is already full.
steal: A Pay button that names the total.

lanes.flow: Held slot, one Pay button, confirmation

screens.step: Checks out with the slot held

notes.t: "Your held slot" shows "Tmrw 8am · 11 min left", so checkout needs no slot choice at all.
One screen holds address, items, delivery, total and "Pay $26.80", which matches the Total line.
The "11 min left" countdown keeps time pressure on the customer while they pay.
The confirmation repeats "Arrives Tmrw 8am" and "$26.80", the slot and total from screen 1.
"Track order" is the only next action offered after the order.

clarity.why: One screen and one button, though the countdown competes for attention.

speed.why: Checkout is a single tap on Pay because the slot is already held.

transparency.why: Full breakdown and the hold time left are both shown.

trust.why: The confirmation matches the checkout figures exactly.

engagement.why: Track order gives a clear next step after paying.

lanes.verdict: Checkout is one tap because the slot was settled earlier, but a running countdown hangs over it.
well: Held slot carried into checkout.
Pay button names the amount.
Confirmation repeats slot and total.
wrong: The countdown adds pressure at the moment of payment.
steal: Carry a held slot into checkout so it needs no slot choice.
A confirmation that repeats arrival time and total.

lanes.flow: Late error, then back to slot and totals

screens.step: Places the order, hits an error

notes.t: "Cannot place order" with "2 items are no longer available" appears on Review order, after slot and payment are set.
The error does not name the two items, and its only action is "Back".

screens.step: Goes back to the slot and totals

notes.t: The total moves from $50.85 on screen 1 to $50.20 here, and this breakdown has no promo line.
The slot the customer had, "Tmrw 6pm", is still selected after going back.

clarity.why: The error does not say which items or what to do about them.

speed.why: The order fails at the last step and sends the customer back a screen.

transparency.why: Unnamed items and a total that changes with no line explaining it.

trust.why: A late failure followed by a total that moves without a reason.

engagement.why: Back is offered, nothing helps the customer recover the shop.

lanes.verdict: Keeps the chosen slot after an error, but fails late and changes the total without saying why.
well: The slot survives the trip back.
wrong: Stock failure at the last step.
Error does not name the items.
Total changes with no explanation.
steal: Keep the customer's slot when they are sent back.

lanes.flow: Slot at checkout, then Place order fails

notes.t: The slot is chosen only at checkout, and "Today 6pm is full" in red is the first slot news.
"Total $61.20" sits above Place order with no delivery or item lines on this screen.

screens.step: Place order fails at the last step

notes.t: "Cannot place order" with "2 items are no longer available" appears after Place order, the last step.
The error does not name the two items, and its only action is "OK", with no swap or route to the basket.
The total reads $61.20 on both screens, so it still counts the two items that are unavailable.

clarity.why: The error names no items and OK leaves the next step unclear.

speed.why: The order fails at the last tap, after slot and payment are set.

transparency.why: No breakdown at checkout, and the total ignores the missing items.

trust.why: The customer learns about missing stock only when the order is refused.

engagement.why: The error offers only OK; no route to fix the basket is shown.

lanes.verdict: Saved address and card make checkout short, but it fails at the last tap and gives no way out.
well: Address and card are saved.
A full slot is flagged in red before choosing.
wrong: Stock failure at Place order.
Error names no items and offers only OK.
Slot chosen last.

best.why: The held slot carries into a one screen checkout with the amount on the Pay button.
Two short screens with saved details and a Pay button that names the total.

patterns.name: The amount is on the button
patterns.text: The pay button names the same figure as the Total line.

patterns.name: Saved address and card
patterns.text: Delivery address and payment card are already filled in at checkout.

anti.name: Stock failure at the last step
anti.text: The order is refused for unavailable items after slot and payment are set.

anti.name: An error that names nothing
anti.text: The customer is told two items are gone but not which ones.

anti.name: Slot chosen last
anti.text: The customer meets a full slot only at checkout.

ideal.name: Arrive with the slot held
ideal.text: The slot picked earlier shows at checkout with the time it is held for.

ideal.name: One screen to pay
ideal.text: Address, card, breakdown and a Pay button that names the total.

ideal.name: Confirm what was promised
ideal.text: The confirmation repeats arrival time and total.

gaps.title: The order fails at Place order
gaps.today: After slot and payment, Cannot place order says 2 items are no longer available, names neither, offers only OK and keeps the $61.20 total.
gaps.fix: Check stock when the basket opens; if an item still sells out at checkout, name it and offer swaps on that screen.

gaps.title: The slot is chosen last
gaps.today: Choose a slot appears at checkout, where Today 6pm is already full.
gaps.fix: Pick and hold the slot before the basket and carry it into checkout.

gaps.title: Place order does not name the amount
gaps.today: The button reads Place order, with the total on a line above it and no breakdown.
gaps.fix: A Pay button that names the total, above a short breakdown.

principles.name: Start from last time
principles.text: A returning customer's first screen should offer their last shop, not the catalogue.

principles.name: Bad news first
principles.text: Stock and price changes belong at the top of the basket, never in an error at Place order.

principles.name: Settle the slot early
principles.text: A slot held before the basket turns checkout into one tap.

principles.name: Every number has a line
principles.text: Totals, delivery charges and offers each appear where the customer decides, and agree from screen to screen.
